tools.name: list_characters
tools.description: List the bitHuman house characters that can speak. Each has an id (pass it as `character` to make_character_video or talk_to_character), a name, a short description, a picture URL and `talk` (true when talk_to_character is open for it). No arguments and read-only; one call per conversation is enough

tools.name: make_character_video
tools.description: Make a short video of one bitHuman house character saying `text` word for word, in its own voice. Returns video_url (an MP4 that plays inline and expires after 7 days), duration_seconds and share_url, labelled AI character. Example: {"character": "wise-pup", "text": "Welcome back! Ready for today's

tools.name: talk_to_character
tools.description: Open a live voice conversation with one bitHuman house character in a player in the chat. The user presses Start and speaks through the microphone; the character answers out loud. A conversation lasts up to 60 seconds (max_seconds), then ends by itself; call again for another. Returns session_url: w

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_characters, talk_to_character · Public sink: make_character_video · Destructive: make_character_video.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_characters, talk_to_character · Public sink: make_character_video · Destructive: make_character_video

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_characters" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
